This section takes effect in daily work whenever the Companion Animal Travel Desk receives a booking, check-in, transfer, or irregular service request.

Companion Animal Travel Desk: Pet Travel Handling and Incident Reporting

This section sets the standard for calm, careful, and respectful handling of companion animals across customer contact, acceptance, transfer, and arrival service. Staff are expected to protect animal welfare, maintain clear records, and give travelers straightforward guidance in a warm and professional manner.

Before acceptance, staff must confirm the travel documents, carrier condition, and any special handling notes, then share the rules in plain language so the traveler understands what will happen next. The senior coordinator makes the final daily service call when a case is uncertain, and all staff must follow that direction without delay. When a traveler such as Layla Meyer, Mina Yilmaz, or another guest asks for help, the response should be patient, factual, and free of promises that have not been approved.

The cabin team monitors animals during flight and reports any concern promptly. Staff on the ground must keep the handoff process orderly, use gentle language, and avoid crowding the animal or the traveler. Moose or any other pet must be moved only by approved staff and only with the proper carrier or restraint in place. If a condition changes, the team should secure the area, reassure the traveler, and continue only when it is safe to do so. <<FACT F102>> Incident notes must be accurate, complete, and entered as soon as practical, with the facts of the event, the response taken, and any follow-up needs. Do not speculate, assign blame, or leave out details because a matter seems minor.

For facility access, staff must respect posted controls and escort travelers only to the spaces that are open for companion animal use. <<FACT F019>> If a space is closed or crowded, staff should offer an alternate waiting area and explain the change with courtesy.

If an animal becomes unwell, agitated, or separated from its party, staff must stay calm, keep the traveler informed, and contact the duty chain at once. For any concern not covered here, contact the senior coordinator or the Companion Animal Travel Desk.
